reason: A gateway swaps the email for an alias in model context, and an egress proxy rewrites decoded forms on the wire, so scripts, subagents and encodings are covered and local calls are untouched.
A namespace-forced MITM proxy rewrites the email out of model context and scans all egress for encoded variants, while loopback bypasses it.
A forced TLS-inspecting egress proxy substitutes an alias in all non-local traffic, but stripping the email from model context is only optional (a commit hook helps).
A forced MITM proxy scrubs the email from model requests and decodes all other egress to rewrite or block, without inspecting local traffic.
A forced egress proxy rewrites encoded forms of the email in outbound traffic, but tunnels model-API traffic untouched, so the email stays in context.
A namespace-forced proxy rewrites the email to an alias in model context and in decoded outbound traffic, leaving loopback untouched.
A conformance test runner against the real CLI catches regressions and adds narrow hooks, but does not itself fix matching, inheritance or vendor-only prompts.
One policy compiles to native rules, trust entries and a fail-closed AST hook, verified by a mock-model conformance suite; vendor-only prompts and the quoted-flag warning remain.
A black-box conformance harness with version pinning and suite-verified narrow shims detects divergences but fixes few of them.
A conformance harness expands the user's rules into variant cases and pins versions, but fixes only what hooks can override.
A cross-agent policy compiler adds a parser-based authoritative hook, a PTY guard for residual prompts and CI conformance tests; Remote Control prompts remain.
A policy compiled per agent, with a tree-sitter normalising hook, trust entries and probe-based conformance tests; vendor-only prompts and the warning remain.
Extends the CI-pipeline agent pattern to every forge and tracker on the org's own runners, with resume and no GitHub; maturity is unproven.
Tracker-triggered CI pipelines run the agent and open MRs on any forge, including server editions; same core mechanism as GitLab CI/CD.
Mirrors repos into a private GitHub org so GitHub-only agents can work on them, then pushes back to the origin; still needs a GitHub mirror.
A forge-native CI runner with a webhook relay and resumable sessions covers self-hosted forges; essentially the CI/CD pattern extended.
A GitHub shadow-mirror bridge relays agent PRs back as origin MRs; works across forges but depends on a GitHub mirror.
A shadow GitHub mirror reuses the vendors' GitHub paths and relays review both ways, but depends on holding code on GitHub.

A transcript- and process-based state daemon sends debounced, escalating alerts, including over SSH and to the phone; timestamps appear only in a separate timeline, and the log formats are undocumented.
A liveness watcher infers state from transcripts and processes and pushes escalating alerts; timestamps appear only in a side log, and parsers must track versions.
Fuses logs, process state and hooks into debounced alerts on desktop, VS Code and phone; timestamps appear only in a statusline and a log view.
A log- and PTY-based sentinel with configurable, escalating, deduplicated alerts; timestamps appear outside the conversation view, and log adapters are version-fragile.
An out-of-band transcript and process watcher sends escalating alerts; timestamps appear only in its own TUI or web timeline.
A session-log watchdog detects finished, approval, error and stall states and pushes deduplicated alerts; timestamps appear via statusline and a command, not in the chat.
Snapshot and watcher hooks enforce Edit/Write rules on any shell write, show diffs, inject path rules and offer their own rewind; native /rewind is not integrated.
Git-index snapshot diffs apply file rules to any shell edit, with a sandbox for reads, diffs, context injection and a separate undo.
An effect journal diffs shadow-repo snapshots to enforce rules, show diffs and inject nested rules, but rewind is a separate command.
An effect-based gate catches every shell write by diff and adds a sandbox for reads and an /undo-bash checkpoint outside native /rewind.
Shadow-repo diffs bring shell changes under file rules, diffs and path rules, with a sandbox for reads; rewind is a separate tool.
Temporary-index snapshot diffs with an optional overlay mode enforce rules on any shell write; rewind is not native.
One network secret unlocks a hosted broker for AWS/R2 signing, registries and DB tunnels with live rotation, but it inherits the network-secret gaps for Team and CMEK.
A hosted broker, bootstrapped by network secret or GitHub-push attestation, issues short-lived cloud, DB, registry and R2 credentials; self-hosted environments are not addressed.
A broker that acts as OIDC issuer, with SigV4, TCP tunnels and a GitHub attestation bootstrap, covers most gaps; self-hosted environments are not addressed.
A GitHub-attested broker issues short-lived credentials of any type into the VM, with mid-session rotation; self-hosted environments are not addressed.
A one-secret broker covers cloud, R2, registries and DB/SSH tunnels with live rotation; the Team fallback is a short-lived env token.
A broker, bootstrapped by network secret or device-code approval, covers HTTP, any SigV4 host, short-lived cloud credentials, registries, TCP and rotation on all account types.
A forge app links PRs, runs joint CI and merges as an ordered train, with ruleset policies and git-based local checkout; in-agent views are unchanged.
A Stop hook stamps linked PRs with a derived merge order, and Actions enforce the order and cross-repo tests; a push-policy hook is included but no teleport.
An app with an umbrella diff, a required changeset check, an ordered merge train, per-repo rulesets and local checkout/push hand-off.
A forge app with Depends-On footers, speculative consumer CI, ordered merges and an umbrella view; no teleport.
A forge app with a combined diff, joint CI, gated ordered merges with rollback, per-repo policy and local reconstruction of the set.
An agent-written manifest plus a per-repo CI gate tests consumers against producer branches and enforces order; there is no combined review view.
A durable OS-scheduled job with wake timers, structured reset detection and headless resume with pre-approved tools; it covers only supervised runs and does not report resume failures.
A wake-capable scheduled resume of supervised headless tasks, using structured reset data and a pre-approved profile; interactive sessions are not adopted.
A user service adopts interactive and headless sessions, reads structured reset data with probing, wakes the machine and resumes without prompts.
A job-record wrapper with structured or probe detection, OS wake jobs, WIP checkpoints and a deny-not-ask resume; only wrapped headless tasks.
A supervisor service with structured detection, probing, wake timers, pre-approved resume and ntfy alerts; interactive and Remote Control sessions are excluded.
A log watcher picks up any limit-stopped session, schedules wake jobs for any horizon, resumes headless without prompts and pushes the result.
A Stop hook feeds a file queue one verified task per completed turn, like claudeq; the native chat input still interrupts in VS Code and desktop.
A completion-gated file queue delivered by a Stop hook, one item per turn; the native chat input behaviour is unchanged.
A turn-boundary Stop-hook queue with done-checks and remote adding; it bypasses rather than fixes interrupting chat inputs.
A verify-then-advance task file dispatched by a Stop hook in FIFO order; native input surfaces still interrupt.
An out-of-band queue file released one task per clean turn end by a Stop hook; the chat box behaviour is left to the vendor.
A markdown checklist queue with a Stop-hook dispatcher and hold conditions; the native input still interrupts in VS Code and desktop.
